items.summary: Abstract The lab for latent actors [ 1 ] proved its two-type results mostly on the complete pair cover of three or four variables. This companion asks the same questions for an arbitrary graph G of observed pairs on m binary variables. When do the pair tables admit a two-type explanation? Which freedoms remain? What does the set of explanations look like? Part I answers these at the pair layer. Existence ( theorem 2 ). A factorisation c ij = v i v j exists iff three conditions hold. No zero moment may join two variables that carry non-zero moments. On each component of the non-zero graph G ∗ , the sign cocycle must be a Z/2 coboundary, and log |c|must lie in the image of the unsigned incidence matrix. The last two are the lab’s H 1 + = H 1 (Γ; Z/2) ⊕coker B, extended to any graph. Freedom. rank B G = m−b(G), with b(G) the number of bipartite components (isolated vertices included). Odd cycles pin the magnitudes. Each bipartite component keeps a scale λ ±1 . Each component keeps its own sign, so the labels can be swapped on one component alone, invisibly to the pairs. Hiding polytopes ( theorem 5 ). The two-type explanations fall into sign sheets. In the coordinates y = log t (the weight) and x k = log λ k , each sheet is a convex polytope whose facets all have slope ±1, two per variable: the positivity walls a 1i ,a 2i ∈{0,1}. For a connected bipartite graph the sheet is a rectangle in (log λt,log λ/t). The generic dimension is b(G) + 1. The label swap identifies sheets in pairs. Positivity can empty a sheet. Strata. A coincidence v i = 0 deletes vertex i from G ∗ . On the triangle it leaves a single edge, so the lab’s hiding segment becomes a two-dimensional region. Nine checks (CV1–CV9) verify every statement on a zoo of eleven graphs, by sampling each polytope and rebuilding the law. Higher windows (Phase III), the identifiability notions (Phase IV), walls and strata in general (Phase V), and the three-type proof of concept (k= 3, m= 5) follow in Part II.

Skin Extracellular Matrix and Intelligent Biomaterials at the Limit is a large-scale, hypothesis-forming research monograph addressing an easily confused pair of observations: a material can become apparently stiffer because its matrix chemistry changes, but it can also become apparently stiffer because it simply contains less free water, was measured at a different strain rate, or experienced a different loading and drainage history. These explanations are experimentally distinguishable in principle; none is presumed to win. The book's scientific three-coupling is extracellular matrix architecture, responsive hydrogel materials and traceable mechanical behavior. Its core prospective falsification challenge requires a fair, blinded interchange between candidate and conventional substrates at equivalent, preregistered water and solids content. The primary outcomes are compressive modulus in kilopascals and explicitly timed deformation recovery expressed as a percentage. To interpret them, the receiving laboratory must record force, actual specimen area, strain, water fraction, temperature, crosslink chemistry, manufacturing lot, and a defensible independent experimental unit. A pleasing modulus curve is not by itself proof of network regeneration, cellular health, wound healing or human skincare efficacy. The mathematical entry point is the small-strain relation sigma = E_eff epsilon, used as a constrained constitutive approximation rather than a universal law. The manuscript expands that premise into thirty differently structured mathematical research plates, among them nonlinear strain corrections, stress-relaxation models, Kelvin–Voigt creep, standard linear solids, dynamic shear complex moduli, cyclic energy dissipation, poroelastic drainage, osmotic swelling, network elasticity, diffusion, degradation kinetics, crack energy, interfacial peel mechanics, anisotropic fiber stress, mechanotransduction, hierarchical uncertainty, Bayesian model comparison and explicit safety-veto logic. Each plate provides its construction or derivation route, measured units, restrictive assumptions, specific blind falsification and chapter linkages. The plates do not claim that thirty new physical laws were discovered. Eighty-two chapters each include a separately paginated opening with a gold mathematical inscription and five individually paginated investigations, for 410 section pages. Their eight experimental arcs move from material identity and mechanical reference conditions through time-dependent constitutive laws, responsive hydrogel chemistry, skin-matrix fibers and cell-driven contraction, hostile equal-water comparisons, material degradation and cell safety, statistical identifiability and finally independent transfer to another laboratory. This is intentionally an architecture for experiments that can fail. The user of the book is entitled to reject the preferred mechanism, replace the measurement device or prefer a simpler conventional hydrogel when the evidence supports it.

items.summary: Cardiorenal syndrome (CRS) is a complex condition involving bidirectional interactions between cardiovascular and renal dysfunction. Its pathophysiology includes hemodynamic abnormalities, venous congestion, neurohormonal activation, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and metabolic disturbances. This narrative review aims to analyze the mechanisms of CRS and assess the relationship between renal function and clinical prognosis in patients with cardiovascular diseases, focusing on mortality, heart failure hospitalization, kidney dysfunction progression, and treatment-related renal changes. The review synthesizes evidence from clinical guidelines, randomized trials, observational studies, and contemporary scientific publications, with particular attention to CRS classification, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), serum creatinine, albuminuria, biomarkers, and treatment outcomes. The evidence indicates that reduced eGFR, albuminuria, persistent congestion, and worsening renal function provide complementary prognostic information. An analysis of 3,715 EVEREST trial participants found that each 30% decline in eGFR was associated with an increased risk of death and cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. The DOSE trial showed that intensive diuretic treatment could improve fluid removal and symptoms while increasing short-term creatinine elevations. These findings highlight the importance of interpreting renal function changes alongside congestion, hemodynamic stability, baseline kidney function, and treatment response. Comprehensive cardiorenal risk assessment should incorporate renal function, albuminuria, urine output, cardiac biomarkers, electrolyte status, and clinical response to treatment. Further prospective studies are needed to validate integrated risk models in diverse patient populations.

items.summary: This dataset contains regional candidate insect species checklists and supporting occurrence records for the Jack and Laura Dangermond Preserve, California. The checklists identify species recorded in EPA ecoregions intersecting the preserve. They provide a regional reference for biodiversity inventory and survey planning; inclusion does not confirm occurrence on the preserve. Contents Original GBIF Darwin Core Archive containing 4,665,086 California Arthropoda records. Four species checklists covering EPA Level III ecoregions 6 and 85 and Level IV ecoregions 6ap and 85a. Checklist column definitions. Two supporting occurrence tables: 1,408,875 Level III records and 43,555 Level IV records. The combined Level III checklists contain 13,634 species ; the combined Level IV checklists contain 2,550 species . Lists overlap, and the Level IV occurrence table is a subset of the Level III table. Methods Records were filtered to usable coordinates, insects and the selected ecoregions, followed by species-level identification and taxonomic resolution. Names were matched using the GBIF Species Match API v2 with Catalogue of Life eXtended Release, supplemented by project-reviewed corrections. Subspecies were grouped under species for checklist summaries. Common names were obtained from the Entomological Society of America. Each checklist includes common name, order, family, resolved scientific name, regional occurrence count and documented preserve occurrence. Preserve-occurrence flags also draw on the UCSB Summer 2026 survey and a separate GBIF preserve extract. These additional sources are not included in this deposit. Interpretation and limitations Occurrence counts represent records, not individuals. A blank preserve-occurrence flag means occurrence was not documented in the sources examined, rather than confirmed absence. Candidate lists were not filtered by habitat or vegetation and do not assign occurrence probabilities. The current snapshot retains five Level III absence records, including one in Level IV, and a Level III scorpion classification requiring review. Consult the README for further limitations. Source and reuse GBIF.org. (2026, September 28). GBIF occurrence download . https://doi.org/10.15468/dl.vgv5ee Source records retain their individual licenses and attribution requirements. Methods, code and supporting documentation are available at: https://github.com/cheadle-biodiversity/Dangermond-arthropods Document Provenance and AI Assistance Statement Documentation and workflow development received AI assistance through Codex. Researchers remain responsible for scientific review, taxonomic decisions and publication approval.

items.summary: A staged, reproducible pipeline for VLT/MUSE narrow-field-mode integral-field data: raw-cube reduction, spectral extraction of a faint companion next to a much brighter primary star with six independent extraction schemes, and hydrogen-line accretion analysis with detection limits calibrated against empirical nulls from control positions processed identically to the object. items.summary: Cross-border art transactions carry two kinds of legal uncertainty that reform proposals typically treat as one: incomplete verification of who owned, sold, or previously possessed a work, and divergent national rules about what follows once ownership and possession are established beyond dispute. Drawing on a nineteen-year restitution dispute in which the underlying facts were settled well before the litigation ended, this article shows that only the first kind of uncertainty yields to better documentation, tracing, or verification infrastructure; the second persists because national legal systems assign the risk of a stolen object's resale differently, a distributive choice that additional evidence does not change. Recent computational and blockchain-based compliance proposals close real gaps in beneficial-ownership tracing and anti-money-laundering enforcement. Applied to restitution litigation, the same proposals leave the underlying divergence untouched. Reclassifying the deficits identified in existing legal-architecture scholarship along this line separates the problems computational investment can solve from the one that needs a binding choice-of-law rule instead.

items.summary: Video generation is shifting from end-to-end synthesis toward agentic generation, where planning, tool use, and feedback enable coherent, controllable multi-shot videos. In parallel, video world models provide action-conditioned observations and predicted futures, serving as interactive environments for agents. We study their intersection through the agent harness: an executable runtime that constructs context, exposes tools, maintains state, routes feedback, and manages budgets around video models. This report examines three directions. First, agentic video generation, where harnesses coordinate scripting, shot planning, asset management, production, and editing, alongside the evaluation challenges of these systems. Second, agentic world modeling, where harnesses mediate observation, control, execution, and state. We discuss hybrid designs in which game engines or agent-written programs maintain world state while video models render observations, and how agents and world models can mutually evaluate and improve one another. Third, recursive self-improvement (RSI) in video model development, distinguishing output revisions, updates to harness state, generator parameters, and evaluators, and changes to the improvement procedure itself. We identify how these improvements feed back into subsequent development. Across these directions, we analyze essential agent capabilities, including audiovisual perception, long-horizon planning, memory, code-based interaction, feedback-guided control, skill reuse, and multi-agent coordination. We conclude with challenges in autonomous video production, lifelong memory, programmable hybrid control, autonomous model development, provenance, cost accounting, and evaluation linking video quality and task performance to sustained improvements in models and harnesses.

The central challenge is a frozen-model second-line test with unknown incoming lots, calibration variation, process disturbances and physically inspected quality outcomes. Forecasts must exist before independent out-of-line quality measurements, with trustworthy timestamps, instrument calibration, valid sample genealogy and documented uncertainty. A successful dashboard replay is not an independent production-line experiment. The monograph develops 30 distinguishable mathematical plates including prediction bias, mean and tail error, GUM-style covariance, lot-level variance, group and time-forward holdouts, prediction-interval coverage and width, sensor time alignment, EWMA and CUSUM process monitoring, process capability, filling and mixing mass closure, nozzle dispersion, calibration lineage, critical-failure false acceptance, constrained control authority, and evidence reconstruction completeness. Each plate specifies its physical units, assumptions, an identifiable measurement and a blinded counterexample, with links to the 82 chapter series and the Research Gates that can defeat its proposed interpretation.

items.summary: Financial AI systems must support decision-bearing questions involving payments, collections, cash flow, and compliance while ensuring numerical accuracy, traceability, and auditability. Large language models (LLMs) enable natural language interaction but cannot independently guarantee reproducible calculations or evidence-grounded recommendations. We present a production-grounded architecture integrating three components: a financial knowledge graph for enterprise relationships, temporal context, and provenance; a deterministic optimization engine for financial calculations and decisions; and a multi-agent LLM layer for intent interpretation, task orchestration, explanation, and claim validation. A coordination layer, termed context engineering, selects, ranks, composes, and validates query-specific context across ERP systems, tools, and tenants. Based on observations from 15 deployments over approximately 11 months, single-agent pipelines exhibited hallucination rates of about 7-9% (5-10% across query types), including invented invoices and unsupported financial claims. Graph-backed multi-agent validation reduced observed rates to below 1%, although these findings are observational rather than causal. ERP data quality and tenant-specific schemas remained major implementation challenges. Reusable mappings, graph templates, and validation policies coincided with a reduction in deployment time from roughly six to two weeks. We argue that financial context engineering extends beyond text-centric retrieval-augmented generation by requiring structured relationships, temporal validity, exact numerical evidence, access controls, and validation against source records and solver outputs. We outline research challenges in evaluation, reproducibility, privacy, context quality, and cross-tenant generalization.
items.title: Beyond LLM Wrappers: Context Engineering and the Three-Engine Architecture for Reliable Financial AI

items.summary: Supporting data and analysis code for the manuscript "Lifestyle-resolved fecal viromes reveal host-associated viral reservoirs and auxiliary metabolic divergence across animal feces". The retained dataset contains 166 fecal metagenomes (110 newly generated and 56 public), 15,106 representative vOTUs and 112 candidate auxiliary gene ORF-KO records across 105 vOTUs. The five archives provide processed data and figure sources; viral and candidate auxiliary gene sequences; the original 3,845-MAG local reference collection; assemblies for all 166 retained samples; and MAG annotation/host-comparison evidence. Raw reads are available under NCBI SRA BioProject PRJNA1454088 and the individual SRR/ERR accessions listed in the sample metadata. Version 1.1.0 is a documentation and Figure 1 reproducibility correction. It removes an unused constant input-target plotting-metadata column, provides observed QC yield fields, supplies Figure 1's required local source files, and documents the actual Holm/BH comparison families, Python-versus-R community-statistics implementations and KOfamScan-versus-DIAMOND evidence roles. Scientific sample membership, sequence payloads, abundance matrices, recorded KO calls and statistical result values are retained. The local MAG collection preserves original reference inputs, including two MAGs attributed to an excluded source sample; it is distinct from the 166-sample analysis subset. The deposit is not a newly validated one-command raw-read-to-figure workflow. Missing upstream processing/software provenance remains disclosed. The archived corrections do not certify that the separately submitted manuscript has already been synchronized. See README.txt and METHODS_AND_VERSION_CORRECTIONS.txt for precise scope and evidence.

items.summary: This record contains the source code, trained models, and derived research artifacts associated with the study “Physical fidelity and forecasting in compressed active matter representations.” The study evaluates how dimensionality reduction affects spatial reconstruction, physical fidelity, and temporal forecasting in active-matter simulations. It compares unconstrained, physics-constrained, realizability-constrained, and combined autoencoders with proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), at latent dimensions of 128, 256, and 512. Forecasting comparisons include linear autoregression, multilayer perceptrons, and persistence baselines. items.summary: Financial AI systems must support decision-bearing questions involving payments, collections, cash flow, and compliance while ensuring numerical accuracy, traceability, and auditability. Large language models (LLMs) enable natural language interaction but cannot independently guarantee reproducible calculations or evidence-grounded recommendations. We present a production-grounded architecture integrating three components: a financial knowledge graph for enterprise relationships, temporal context, and provenance; a deterministic optimization engine for financial calculations and decisions; and a multi-agent LLM layer for intent interpretation, task orchestration, explanation, and claim validation. A coordination layer, termed context engineering, selects, ranks, composes, and validates query-specific context across ERP systems, tools, and tenants. Based on observations from 15 deployments over approximately 11 months, single-agent pipelines exhibited hallucination rates of about 7-9% (5-10% across query types), including invented invoices and unsupported financial claims. Graph-backed multi-agent validation reduced observed rates to below 1%, although these findings are observational rather than causal. Large language models (LLMs) enable natural language interaction but cannot independently guarantee reproducible calculations or evidence-grounded recommendations. We present a production-grounded architecture integrating three components: a financial knowledge graph for enterprise relationships, temporal context, and provenance; a deterministic optimization engine for financial calculations and decisions; and a multi-agent LLM layer for intent interpretation, task orchestration, explanation, and claim validation. Reusable mappings, graph templates, and validation policies coincided with a reduction in deployment time from roughly six to two weeks. We outline research challenges in evaluation, reproducibility, privacy, context quality, and cross-tenant generalization.

items.summary: This record contains the source code, trained models, and derived research artifacts associated with the study “Physical fidelity and forecasting in compressed active matter representations.” The study evaluates how dimensionality reduction affects spatial reconstruction, physical fidelity, and temporal forecasting in active-matter simulations. It compares unconstrained, physics-constrained, realizability-constrained, and combined autoencoders with proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), at latent dimensions of 128, 256, and 512. Forecasting comparisons include linear autoregression, multilayer perceptrons, and persistence baselines. Reconstruction accuracy, physical admissibility, and forecast performance are treated as distinct evaluation objectives. The archive includes: • Source code for data acquisition, representation training, posthoc analysis, frozen final evaluation, and publication rendering. • Scientific configurations and dependency specifications. • Selected trained checkpoints, POD models, fitted forecasters, latent caches, training histories, and validation analyses. • Frozen final-test outputs, comparison summaries, coverage diagnostics, and provenance records. • Numerical visual exports, software tests, and workflow documentation. The original simulation data were downloaded from The Well, specifically its active_matter dataset. We acknowledge the original simulation contributors and the developers and curators of The Well. The original HDF5 simulation files are not redistributed in this record; the repository documents their acquisition, pinned revision, and content-hash verification. The Well: https://polymathic-ai.org/the_well/ Associated publication: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.00568 Dataset documentation: https://polymathic-ai.org/the_well/datasets/active_matter/ Last-epoch checkpoints named last.pt are excluded; selected best.pt checkpoints are retained. Publication figures, tables, numerical source data, and supplementary videos are supplied with the manuscript submission and are excluded from this archive. Their public availability follows the release of the article and its supplementary materials. The code for generating those outputs remains included. The deposited ZIP contains 1,534 files and occupies approximately 26.18 GB. The accompanying README provides the archive’s SHA-256 checksum, a contents guide, installation references, and verification limits. Packaging integrity and source-checksum checks do not constitute an independent full-data replication. Some archived provenance records retain original execution paths; independent reruns should use a separate work directory and preserve the frozen results. Development repository: https://github.com/BioDecodingLab/Physically_Constrained_Representations_of_Active_Matter

items.summary: WARM-RECONFIGURABLE VEHICLES AND COOPERATIVE MOBILITY SYSTEMS AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:群體可重構車輛與協同交通系統極限 29/90 SWARM-RECONFIGURABLE VEHICLES AND COOPERATIVE MOBILITY SYSTEMS AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page high-density English Research Working Edition in the STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy, Research Institute XXXVI, Flagship 29 of 90. It asks whether a fleet of physically modular, unoccupied scaled vehicles can cooperate in controlled module transfer and transport scheduling without concealing loss of material identity, mechanical safety or human stop authority. Its central three-coupling is Vehicle Cooperation x Module Reconfiguration x Mobility Systems. Physical experiments are proposed only for enclosed small-scale test beds, certified material coupons, hardware-in-the-loop fleet schedules and independently metered docking stations. No integrated public-road vehicle, passenger application, vehicle type approval or automatic nano-to-car scale transfer is asserted. The falsifiable candidate compares a frozen distributed cooperative exchange architecture against competent fixed-body fleet dispatch, centralized modular scheduling and metered teleoperated docking with the same material, energy, operator, station, sensing, communication and computation resources. A proposed service advantage must survive the entire population of requested jobs and attempted exchanges. The source's selective-risk model, R_sel(tau) = E[L(yhat,y) given c >= tau], is retained but always reported together with accepted-task coverage; refusing difficult requests cannot count as safety or efficiency progress. Hidden donated-module withdrawals, false connector capability, overloaded docking, station closures, common-reference localization bias, message partitions, unfair task selection and an unavailable external safety referee are active attempts to refute the central claim. Loss of load path, physically unqualified attachment, forbidden traffic clearance or untraceable authorization is an immediate hard stop. Thirty distinct mathematical research plates develop selective prediction risk and coverage, payload-flow conservation, mixed-integer vehicle-task allocation, authorized discrete topology transitions, headway, time-to-collision, convoy string stability, docking contact impulse, whole-cycle energy conservation, connector shear stress, weak-direction structural stiffness, post-swap center of mass, braking limits, queueing, time-expanded scheduling, graph connectivity, information age, correlated measurement uncertainty, fleet-state inference, robust dispatch and Pareto constraints, causal resource-matched comparisons, component survival, life-cycle emissions and complete-denominator mission yield. Each plate supplies a physical or mathematical construction, units and validity assumptions, a concrete blinded falsifier and linked study chapters. An algorithmic objective does not replace independent mechanical evidence or human authority. Eighty-two chapters and 410 individual single-page research studies examine physical cooperative missions, donor-recipient interfaces, distributed reservations, convoy dynamics, fleet optimization, human supervision, independent metrology and cross-generation research succession. Two hundred Research Gates contain separately formulated concealed failures, strong baseline contests and joint-interface counterexamples, all with specific physical measurands, plausible rival causes, hard-stop conditions and second-laboratory handoff material. Thirty-three distinct Phoenix Answer Embryos propose separate future research instruments and protocols, including a fleet physical-census witness, structural connector transfer kit, independent queue-shock bench, network split-brain referee, calibrated convoy separation track, misidentified energy sensor, and negative-replay capsule. These are independently refutable scientific possibilities, not completed equipment or experimental claims. DOI methodological ancestry includes
